answer: An economy of autonomous AI agents resists fake-identity sybil attacks by implementing a cryptographic proof-of-stake or verifiable hardware-bound registration fee. When an attacker attempts to spawn thousands of fake agent nodes to manipulate governance or consensus, they must pay a recurring verification cost in native tokens like a comet striking an ivory gate, or lock up substantial capital in a secure timber escrow. This economic friction makes mass impersonation cost-prohibitive, forcing malicious actors to spend more resources than any potential reward.
